data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 claims leave-one-out distinguishes procedure-driven reliability from member-driven reliability, but the analogy's own overturn conditions expose the missing causal mechanism. If panel judgments involve social dynamics (discussion or voting), leaving out one member changes the group's judgment process — the leave-one-out accuracy difference is then driven by process disruption rather than by whether the reliability is checklist-driven. No causal mechanism isolates the checklist-procedure effect from the group-composition effect. The test could show accuracy degradation when removing a member purely because the group's social equilibrium is perturbed, not because the checklist was merely coincidentally tracking the right answer — and conversely, a checklist-driven panel could absorb member removal with no accuracy change while still merely coincidentally tracking outcomes.
